old_control.interpretation: Original static one-per-denom gate stranded a required cap while a global dispatch slot was observably idle after the other denom completed all three reads.

original_fixture_fixed_pairs.field_results: Both mappings, required cap, useful native output and both floor capabilities present.

design: After validated bindings, declare exactly three required bits per bound denom, or zero for a validated unbound denom, once before constructing/polling native futures.
Non-clone construction-time RAII retires each slot after cleanup on success/error/drop, including unpolled cancellation; duplicate/absent registrations cannot retire another owner or renew bits.

Keep ordinary one-per-denom admission while peer work remains. Once the peer remaining mask is zero, an otherwise blocked read may bypass its own busy semaphore and queue for the existing global semaphore.

The global two-logical-read bound, global FIFO admission, scoped original deadline and provider pacing/attempt accounting remain intact. No additional global permit, RPC, task, retained queue or cross-poll state is added.
Notify wait is registered/enabled before checking peer completion; no native state mutex is held across await.

Existing completion event adds only native_borrowed_reads, bounded0..6 and incremented after successful global admission plus deadline recheck. It counts logical bypass admissions, never wire delivery.
Actual admission statistics used in controls are cfg(test) only; no production telemetry stream or provider counter change is added.
covered_controls: Same real-HTTP original fixture fails on OLD static gating and passes twice unchanged after the fix.
Symmetric blocked-denom controls: peer three10ms reads finish30ms, then remaining denom may reach logical concurrency2; global peak stays2.
Both denoms hot: neither borrows before original deadline, queued expiry starts no late transport and records no false borrow.
Unregistered peer bits prevent early borrowing before peer future construction; only final of three retirements wakes peer waiters.
Duplicate registration cannot retire original bit; double finish is idempotent; one-shot plan cannot renew retired work.
Validated unbound slots are rejected; unpolled future drop retires only owned work and never first-polls a transport.
Peer error remains an absent observation; completion may free idle capacity without authorizing the rejected field.
No-plan helpers retain original one-per-denom behavior; closed gate cannot be bypassed.
Whole-wrapper43-test FIRST/RETEST also preserves existing scoped-deadline, pause/revocation, future-size/default-stack, provider-health, original-expiry and thirteen-healthy-read controls.

unchanged_bounds.per_denom_after_peer_done: may use existing global capacity, maximum global2

limitations: The historical M7 poll119 cap waited4218ms on its own denom and had646ms logical LCD activity, but its exact provider sequence and whether a global slot was idle remain UNPROVEN. This synthetic reproduction proves a source defect, not retrospective causation.

Global2 and borrowed-read counters refer to logical LCD futures. The13 healthy data wire requests observed here are not a universal wire cap under provider failover; original per-read attempt bounds and identity requests remain unchanged.
No original fields are retained/spliced or given new timestamps. Arbitrary provider outages may still fail closed.
Source tests do not establish hosted CI or live sustained useful-quote acceptance.

After unchanged standalone FIRST/RETEST, the real fixture moved to a focused child test module with the same payloads/delays/bounds, and gained cfg(test) resource assertions. Existing whole-wrapper verifier filter includes all new modules.
independent_review: Parent, telemetry and browser read-only reviews are clean at all three exact final source hashes. Telemetry additionally verified cfg(test) activity accounting is isolated/RAII-balanced and the runtime counter remains bounded/post-admission.
